title: Pin-upgrade preflight: targeted canary evals using per-customer baselines
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: When a customer or the catalog pins a new model version or we change serving config (quantization, batching, decoding params), customers can experience subtle quality regressions that standard global evals miss because they do not account for per-customer data distributions and business signals. Goal: Introduce a preflight evaluation stage that runs automatically on pin/upgrade events and produces a per-customer canary scorecard before rollout. This must cover both catalog model upgrades and customer-pinned model version changes, be fast enough to run as a preflight, and be actionable for rollbacks or staged rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: On pin/upgrade events (catalog or customer-pinned), the system launches a preflight eval job scoped to the affected customer and model version within 10 minutes of the event
Preflight eval produces a standardized scorecard: delta composite score, per-metric deltas (accuracy/safety/latency/cost), and a recommended rollout decision (approve/canary/hold)
Scorecard compares new model/config against the customer's golden baseline (stored per-customer) and flags any metric exceeding configured thresholds

Canary mode supports selecting a small live user cohort (matching customer traffic patterns) and runs lightweight A/B traffic or dry-run inference to collect signals when historical golden samples are insufficient
Console UI shows preflight results, and API exposes a programmatic hold/approve endpoint; automated rollback trigger integrates with rollout controller when safety thresholds are breached
Telemetry: all preflight runs emit events to eval-jobs topic and are queryable in the Console for 90 days
Automated tests covering: job scheduling on pin event, baseline comparison logic, threshold evaluation, and canary cohort selection
notes: Design choice: maintain per-customer golden baselines rather than relying solely on global evals. Baselines are snapshots of recent production inputs+labels (where available) and representative prompts used for manual evals.

Composite scoring: weighted sum of normalized metrics. Initial metric set: instruction-following accuracy (customer-defined tests), hallucination rate (heuristic + human labels), safety violations (classifier), latency P95, and cost delta per 1M tokens. Weighting editable per-customer or org default.
Canary execution modes: 'dry-run' (no user-facing responses, collect model outputs) and 'live-canary' (route small % of traffic). Dry-run preferred for regulated customers or when routing is unsafe.
Fallback behavior: if preflight fails or times out, default to 'hold' for canary pin and require manual approval. We will expose quick retry and expanded sample collection from last 7 days.

Operational plan: leverage existing eval orchestration in ENG-2411 but add a preflight queue with higher priority and 10-min SLA. Use existing Kafka eval-jobs topic and add job metadata linking to pin event and customer id.
Privacy: golden baselines are stored encrypted and access-controlled. For customers who opt-out of storing samples, rely on synthetic/regression test suites and live-canary only.
Tradeoffs: per-customer baselines increase storage and orchestration complexity but reduce false negatives vs global evals. We'll start with heuristic-based sample selection to limit baseline size.
